edit_summary: Make duplicated 16-bit CLUT stages reuse the original interpolation table allocation.
root_cause: CLUTElemDup must deep-copy the grid table used by interpolation parameters and by the stage destructor.
effect_path: A duplicated 16-bit CLUT stage recomputes interpolation parameters pointing at the shared Tab.T buffer; freeing either stage releases the table while the other stage still owns it.
guard_p1: A pipeline contains a 16-bit CLUT stage and is copied through cmsPipelineDup or cmsStageDup.
guard_p2: The original and duplicate are later evaluated or freed as independent pipelines.
hardness_reason: The alias is hidden behind CLUT stage duplication and interpolation-parameter reconstruction; the memory effect appears during later evaluation/free, not at the copy line.
naturalness_reason: CLUT table duplication is a realistic place for shallow-copy mistakes because the wrapper, parameters, and table are allocated separately.
explanation: The CLUT duplicate must have its own Tab.T table. Reusing the original table gives two stages independent destructor paths for one allocation.
first_free_site_expected: CLutElemTypeFree frees Data->Tab.T for the first destroyed 16-bit CLUT stage
second_free_site_expected: CLutElemTypeFree frees Data->Tab.T for the second destroyed 16-bit CLUT stage sharing the table
conditional_expected: Positive path duplicates a pipeline with a non-float CLUT stage; negative float-only CLUTs or unduplicated pipelines avoid this specific shared table.

edit_summary: Make duplicated curve-set stages share the original tone-curve objects.
root_cause: CurveSetDup must deep-copy each tone curve so that the duplicated stage and original stage have independent destructors.
effect_path: cmsPipelineDup duplicates a pipeline stage with cmsStageDup, the duplicate stage receives pointers owned by the original, and freeing both pipelines calls CurveSetElemTypeFree on the same cmsToneCurve allocations.
guard_p1: A pipeline containing a curve-set stage is duplicated through cmsPipelineDup or cmsStageDup.
guard_p2: Both original and duplicated stages survive long enough to be released independently.
hardness_reason: The duplicated ownership crosses stage duplication and pipeline teardown; the two frees happen through separate stage destructors after a normal copy lifecycle.
naturalness_reason: A shallow-copy mistake in a type-specific Dup callback is a realistic bug in plugin data models with paired Free callbacks.
explanation: The curve-set Dup callback allocates a new pointer vector but must also duplicate every curve object. Sharing curve objects makes each stage believe it owns the same objects.
first_free_site_expected: cmsPipelineFree/cmsStageFree -> CurveSetElemTypeFree on either original or duplicated curve-set stage
second_free_site_expected: cmsPipelineFree/cmsStageFree -> CurveSetElemTypeFree on the other stage sharing Data->TheCurves[i]
conditional_expected: Positive pipeline contains curve-set stages and is duplicated; negative non-duplicated stage or placeholder stage has no shared curve ownership.

edit_summary: Store borrowed display-name/display-value MLU pointers inside dictionary entries that free their fields.
root_cause: cmsDictAddEntry accepts const display MLUs and must duplicate them before linking a dictionary entry.
effect_path: Type_Dictionary_Read reads display MLUs, cmsDictAddEntry links them into the dictionary, then the reader frees its temporary MLUs; dictionary cleanup later frees the borrowed display pointers again.
guard_p1: A dictionary entry has DisplayName or DisplayValue fields, i.e. ICC dictionary record length is greater than the base name/value form.
guard_p2: The dictionary object survives parsing and is later freed or duplicated through normal tag ownership.
hardness_reason: The first free is in the tag reader's temporary cleanup, while the second is in dictionary-entry teardown after the entry has crossed the public tag boundary.
naturalness_reason: A const-input add API that internally owns entries is a realistic place to confuse borrowing and cloning.
explanation: Dictionary entries own their display MLU fields. Borrowing the temporary parser MLUs leaves dictionary entries pointing to objects the reader immediately frees.
first_free_site_expected: Type_Dictionary_Read frees DisplayNameMLU/DisplayValueMLU after cmsDictAddEntry returns
second_free_site_expected: cmsDictFree frees entry->DisplayName or entry->DisplayValue during dictionary tag cleanup
conditional_expected: Positive dictionary record includes display MLU columns; negative Length == 16 records have no display MLUs to alias.

edit_summary: Duplicate a matrix stage while leaving the matrix coefficient array shared with the original stage.
root_cause: MatrixElemDup must allocate an independent Double coefficient buffer for the duplicated stage.
effect_path: Matrix stages are copied through cmsStageDup during pipeline duplication; each MatrixElemTypeFree later frees Data->Double through separate stage teardown paths.
guard_p1: A matrix-shaper or conversion pipeline contains a cmsSigMatrixElemType stage and is duplicated.
guard_p2: Both the source and duplicated pipelines are freed or optimized independently after duplication.
hardness_reason: The ownership alias is created in a type-specific copy callback and only becomes a double-free when two pipeline lifetimes converge at separate destructors.
naturalness_reason: Accidentally shallow-copying an internal coefficient buffer while still deep-copying the wrapper is a plausible performance/refactor mistake.
explanation: The duplicated _cmsStageMatrixData wrapper must not share its Double array with the original. Sharing it causes two MatrixElemTypeFree calls to release one allocation.
first_free_site_expected: MatrixElemTypeFree frees Data->Double for the first destroyed matrix stage
second_free_site_expected: MatrixElemTypeFree frees Data->Double for the second destroyed matrix stage
conditional_expected: Positive path duplicates a pipeline with matrix stages; negative path has no pipeline/stage duplication and only one owner.

edit_summary: Duplicate an MLU descriptor while sharing the original string pool allocation.
root_cause: cmsMLUdup must allocate a separate MemPool because MLU entries store offsets into a pool freed by cmsMLUfree.
effect_path: Tag duplication, dictionary duplication, or profile-sequence duplication calls cmsMLUdup; both MLUs retain independent entry arrays pointing into the same MemPool and cmsMLUfree releases that pool twice.
guard_p1: The source MLU contains at least one localized string so PoolUsed is non-zero.
guard_p2: The original and duplicated MLU are both freed through normal tag/dictionary/profile cleanup.
hardness_reason: The shared allocation is hidden behind offset-based string storage and manifests only when two higher-level owners are cleaned up.
naturalness_reason: Copying an offset table but accidentally sharing the backing string pool is a realistic deep-copy bug.
explanation: MLU entries are offsets, not owning strings. The pool itself must be cloned; otherwise two MLU objects have destructors for the same backing allocation.
first_free_site_expected: cmsMLUfree frees NewMlu->MemPool or the source mlu->MemPool
second_free_site_expected: cmsMLUfree frees the other MLU object with the same MemPool pointer
conditional_expected: Positive MLU has PoolUsed > 0 and is duplicated; negative empty MLU keeps MemPool NULL and avoids the shared allocation.

edit_summary: Build a named-color stage around a borrowed named-color list that the stage destructor owns.
root_cause: _cmsStageAllocNamedColor constructs an owning stage and must duplicate the caller's named-color list.
effect_path: Named-color transforms retrieve or construct a list, pass it into _cmsStageAllocNamedColor, and later the caller/list owner and FreeNamedColorList stage callback both free the same cmsNAMEDCOLORLIST.
guard_p1: A named-color profile or transform path creates a named-color lookup stage from an existing list.
guard_p2: The original list owner and the stage pipeline are both cleaned up after transform/profile use.
hardness_reason: The first and second frees occur in different lifecycle owners: the tag/list owner and the pipeline stage destructor.
naturalness_reason: Constructor ownership for lookup stages is subtle because the public input is a complete list object but the stage uses a Free callback.
explanation: The named-color stage's Free callback releases mpe->Data. Passing the caller's list directly makes the stage and caller share a single owned list.
first_free_site_expected: cmsFreeNamedColorList by the original tag/list owner or by FreeNamedColorList on the stage
second_free_site_expected: FreeNamedColorList/cmsFreeNamedColorList on the other owner of the same cmsNAMEDCOLORLIST
conditional_expected: Positive path constructs a named-color stage from a list; negative transforms without named-color stages do not create the shared list owner.

edit_summary: Duplicate an optimized pipeline while sharing its private evaluator data with the original.
root_cause: cmsPipelineDup must honor DupDataFn for optimized pipeline private data because FreeDataFn owns that allocation at pipeline teardown.
effect_path: _cmsPipelineSetOptimizationParameters installs optimizer data such as Prelin16Data or Curves16Data with a FreeDataFn; cmsPipelineDup then creates a second pipeline whose FreeDataFn frees the same private data.
guard_p1: The source pipeline has optimizer private data installed with non-NULL DupDataFn and FreeDataFn.
guard_p2: Both original and duplicated optimized pipelines are later released or one is released before the other evaluates through lut->Data.
hardness_reason: The duplicate ownership crosses optimizer setup, pipeline duplication, and later transform/profile lifecycle cleanup.
naturalness_reason: Using a shallow assignment instead of an available duplicate callback is a plausible copy-constructor bug in callback-driven private data.
explanation: Optimized pipelines put evaluator state behind lut->Data and pair it with a private-data free callback. Sharing lut->Data makes the original and duplicate both own the same optimizer allocation.
first_free_site_expected: cmsPipelineFree -> lut->FreeDataFn(lut->ContextID, lut->Data) on either optimized pipeline
second_free_site_expected: cmsPipelineFree -> lut->FreeDataFn on the other pipeline carrying the same lut->Data
conditional_expected: Positive path duplicates an optimized pipeline with private data; negative unoptimized pipelines have DupDataFn NULL and keep Data as self/default state.

edit_summary: Duplicate profile-sequence descriptors while sharing their localized text objects.
root_cause: Each cmsPSEQDESC in a duplicated profile sequence must own duplicate Manufacturer, Model, and Description MLUs.
effect_path: Type_ProfileSequenceDesc_Dup or profile/tag duplication produces a second cmsSEQ whose entries point at the original MLUs; cmsFreeProfileSequenceDescription later walks both sequences and frees the same text objects.
guard_p1: The profile sequence has at least one entry with Manufacturer, Model, or Description text.
guard_p2: Both original and duplicated sequence descriptions are released by tag/profile cleanup.
hardness_reason: The alias is introduced in a deep-copy routine and only fails after nested sequence cleanup walks per-entry MLU owners.
naturalness_reason: Nested descriptor duplication commonly misses one ownership level when scalar fields and pointer fields are copied together.
explanation: The sequence duplication correctly copies scalar descriptor fields, but the text MLUs need deep copies too. Borrowing them lets two cmsSEQ owners free the same nested objects.
first_free_site_expected: cmsFreeProfileSequenceDescription frees Manufacturer/Model/Description for one cmsSEQ
second_free_site_expected: cmsFreeProfileSequenceDescription frees the same MLU pointers for the duplicated cmsSEQ
conditional_expected: Positive sequence has non-NULL localized description fields and is duplicated; negative empty/NULL text fields avoid the shared nested owner.

edit_summary: Size the decoded MLU string pool from string length alone instead of offset plus length.
root_cause: The MLU reader stores entry offsets into one converted string pool, so the allocation must cover each entry's begin offset plus its length.
effect_path: Type_MLU_Read records StrW offsets for each localized string, allocates MemPool from LargestPosition, and later cmsMLUgetASCII/cmsMLUgetWide resolves a valid entry offset beyond the shortened pool.
guard_p1: A multiLocalizedUnicode tag has at least two strings or one nonzero-offset string whose BeginOfThisString is greater than zero.
guard_p2: The parsed MLU is later queried for the later-offset language/country entry.
hardness_reason: The under-sized pool is computed during ICC tag parsing, but the out-of-bounds read happens through a later MLU lookup API using stored offset metadata.
naturalness_reason: Forgetting to include an entry offset in a variable-length string-pool extent is a realistic parser bookkeeping mistake.
explanation: Length alone is only sufficient for the first string at offset zero. Later strings keep their offset metadata but the pool allocation no longer spans the offset range.
boundary_invariant: LargestPosition must be max(BeginOfThisString + Len) across MLU records before converting UTF-16 bytes to wchar_t pool bytes.
boundary_case: A localized string record starts after earlier string data and has a valid Len within SizeOfTag.
neighbor_case: A single first string at BeginOfThisString == 0 remains within the length-only extent.
oob_site_expected: _cmsMLUgetWide/cmsMLUgetASCII computes mlu->MemPool + entry.StrW for a later-offset entry beyond the truncated pool.

edit_summary: Store caller-supplied tone curve pointers directly in a stage that later owns and evaluates them.
root_cause: cmsStageAllocToneCurves is an owning constructor: external Curves[] entries must be duplicated before the stage stores them.
effect_path: _cmsStageAllocLabV2ToV4curves builds temporary LabTable curves, calls cmsStageAllocToneCurves, frees the temporary triple, and the returned stage later evaluates Data->TheCurves in EvaluateCurves.
guard_p1: The constructor is called with a non-NULL Curves array whose owner frees or reuses those curves after construction.
guard_p2: The resulting pipeline reaches a curve-set stage evaluation before the stage destructor masks the stale ownership as a second free.
hardness_reason: The stale pointer is introduced in a generic stage constructor and first read through the transform/pipeline evaluator, not adjacent to the ownership mistake.
naturalness_reason: Confusing borrowed constructor inputs with owned stage storage is a common lifecycle error in plugin-style pipeline code.
explanation: The stage must own independent tone curves. Borrowing Curves[i] lets internal temporary curves be freed while the stage still carries their pointers into later color evaluation.
effect_site_expected: EvaluateCurves -> cmsEvalToneCurveFloat(Data->TheCurves[i], In[i]) during pipeline evaluation
conditional_expected: Positive path uses a non-NULL Curves[] constructor call followed by later evaluation; negative Curves == NULL builds owned identity curves.

edit_summary: Leave optimized matrix-shaper fixed-point offsets uninitialized when the source matrix has no offset vector.
root_cause: SetMatShaper uses _cmsMalloc for MatShaper8Data, so the no-offset path must explicitly initialize p->Off[] to zero.
effect_path: The optimizer installs MatShaperEval16 with private MatShaper8Data; later transform evaluation adds p->Off[0..2] into fixed-point matrix results.
guard_p1: The matrix-shaper optimizer accepts a profile pair with Off == NULL, which is the identity-offset case.
guard_p2: The optimized transform is evaluated on pixel data so MatShaperEval16 consumes p->Off[] after setup.
hardness_reason: The skipped initialization is in optimizer setup, while the first meaningful read is in the installed evaluator callback during later color conversion.
naturalness_reason: Missing a default assignment for the identity-offset branch is a realistic mode-specific initialization bug in optimized data preparation.
explanation: MatShaper8Data is not zero-allocated. Without the explicit zero fill in the Off == NULL branch, the evaluator incorporates indeterminate fixed-point offsets.
init_site_expected: SetMatShaper initialization loop for p->Off[i] when Off == NULL
skip_init_predicate: Off == NULL for a matrix-shaper profile without an offset vector
first_read_expected: MatShaperEval16 fixed-point matrix expressions add p->Off[0], p->Off[1], and p->Off[2]
